instructions: Rinse the peppers and dry them very well with a clean towel. Wet peppers spatter in hot oil.
Peel the 2 garlic cloves and halve them lengthwise.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the garlic and stir for about 1 minute, until it sizzles and turns pale gold.
Add the peppers in one layer. Cook, turning them every minute or so, for 5 to 7 minutes, until they're blistered with dark spots all over and soft. Stand back a little. They can pop.
Transfer the peppers and garlic to a plate and sprinkle the 1 tsp flaky salt over them.
Serve right away. Most are mild, but now and then one is hot.
method_notes: Neither version read had ratings and RecipeTin Eats has no padrón peppers, so this follows Spain on a Fork. Both fry whole peppers in olive oil until they blister and soften, then finish them with flaky sea salt and serve them straight away. Spain on a Fork cooks halved garlic in the oil first and goes gently over medium heat for 7 to 8 minutes; The Australian Women's Weekly leaves out the garlic and chars them fast over high heat. This keeps the lead's garlic and meets in the middle at medium-high, and shishito peppers work if you can't find padrón.
